'''Sunomiya Shrine''' (すのみやじんじゃ) is a Shinto shrine in Sunomiya, {{ill|Tateyama, Chiba|ar|تاته ياما (تشيبا)|azb|تاتیاما، چیبا|ce|Татеяма (гӀала)|ceb|Tateyama (lungsod sa Hapon)|cs|Tatejama (město v Čibě)|de|Tateyama (Chiba)|eo|Tatejama (Ĉiba)|es|Tateyama (Chiba)|et|Tateyama|eu|Tateyama (Chiba)|fa|تاته‌یاما، چیبا|fi|Tateyama|fr|Tateyama|gl|Tateyama, Chiba|hu|Tatejama (Csiba)|hy|Տատեյամա|id|Tateyama, Chiba|it|Tateyama|ja|館山市|ko|다테야마시|mg|Tateyama|ms|Tateyama, Chiba|mzn|تاتیاما، چیبا|nl|Tateyama (Chiba)|pl|Tateyama|pt|Tateyama|ro|Tateyama, Chiba|ru|Татеяма (город)|sv|Tateyama|sw|Tateyama, Chiba|tg|Татеяма|th|ทาเตยามะ (จังหวัดชิบะ)|tl|Tateyama, Chiba|tr|Tateyama, Chiba|tt|Татеяма (шәһәр)|uk|Татеяма (Тіба)|ur|تاتییاما، چیبا|uz|Tateyama (Chiba)|vi|Tateyama, Chiba|war|Tateyama, Chiba|zh|館山市|zh_classical|館山市|zh_min_nan|Tateyama-chhī|zh_yue|館山|qid=Q646755}}, {{ill|Chiba Prefecture|Q80011|qid=Q80011}}. It is a candidate shrine for the Engishiki grand shrine "Ame-no-Hirinome-no-Mikoto Shrine" and was formerly ranked as a prefectural shrine.

=== Enshrined deities ===
; Main deity
* '''{{ill|Ame no Hiratome|ja|天比理刀咩命|qid=Q85879124}}'''
: Said to be the consort deity of {{ill|Awa Shrine|Q705547|qid=Q705547}}'s deity and formerly called "Susa no Kami".

; Co-enshrined
* {{ill|Ame-no-Uzume|ar|أمه نو أوزومه|as|আমে-ন′-উজুমে|bcl|Ama-no-Uzume|ca|Ama-no-Uzume|cs|Ama no Uzume|de|Amenouzume|el|Άμε Νο Ουζούμε|eo|Ame no Uzume|es|Ame-no-Uzume|fa|آمه نو اوزومه|fr|Uzume|hr|Ame-no-Uzume|hu|Ame-no-Uzume|id|Ama-no-Uzume|it|Ama-no-Uzume|ja|アメノウズメ|jv|Ama-no-Uzume|ka|ამე-ნო უძუმე|ko|아메노우즈메|mni|ꯑꯃꯦ-ꯅꯣ-ꯎꯓꯨꯃꯦ|no|Ama-no-Uzume|pl|Amenouzume|pt|Ame-no-Uzume-no-Mikoto|ru|Амэ-но удзумэ|simple|Ame-no-Uzume|sv|Uzume|th|อาเมะ โนะ อูซูเมะ|tr|Ame-no-Uzume|uk|Ама-но-Удзуме-но-Мікото|zh|天鈿女命|qid=Q462803|lt=Ame-no-Uzume-no-Mikoto}}
* {{ill|Amatomi no Mikoto|ja|天富命|qid=Q24899653}} (leader of Awa Imibe in the development of Awa)

A historical issue is whether the correct reading is "Hirinome" or "Hiritome," and this has long been discussed in relation to nearby {{ill|Susaki Shrine|ja|洲崎神社|simple|Susaki Shrine|qid=Q11556513}}.

=== History ===
According to shrine tradition, when Ame-no-Tomi-no-Mikoto developed Awa, a shrine was founded here near the sea and called "Susa-gami" or "Sunomiya." In the ''Engishiki Jinmyocho'' (927), the shrine appears as "Kisakigami Ame-no-Hirinome-no-Mikoto Shrine, grand, former name Susa-gami" in Awa District.

Since the Edo period, Sunomiya Shrine and Sunosaki Shrine have disputed which is the Engishiki shrine. In 1872, the Ministry of Doctrine once recognized Sunomiya, then reversed the next year and recognized Sunosaki.

=== Cultural properties ===
=== Tateyama City designated cultural properties ===
* Wooden tenbu statue (Nanbokucho to early Muromachi)
* ''Sunomiya Jinja Engi'' manuscript
* Earthen ritual model objects from the late Kofun period (from former site, To-yama)
* Sunomiya Shrine rice-planting ritual (intangible folk cultural property, held on New Year's morning)

=== Site information ===
* Address: Sunomiya 921, Tateyama, Chiba
* Access: From JR Uchibo Line Tateyama Station, JR bus toward Awa-Shirahama via Kobe; get off at "Sunomiya," then about 2 minutes on foot
